notes: Cross-verse consistency: this chapter puts the construction-supplied copula of a verbless clause on the preposition heading a prepositional predicate in EZK.43.2, EZK.43.3 (twice) and EZK.43.19. EZK.43.8 alone anchored the presentative *there was* on the subject noun קִיר, leaving בֵּין — the head of the clause's predicate — holding only *between*. Rule 49 settles the ordinary copular case on the preposition and says the corpus never moves the copula onto the noun instead; rule 20's presentative sentence puts the dummy *there* on whichever unit bears that copula, whether a nominal anchor or a prepositional predicate. Only the s017 and s018 units change; every other unit is as the verse pass returned it.
